provenance.paper: Hayes, P. J. (1979). The Naive Physics Manifesto; Hayes, P. J. (1985). Naive physics I: ontology for liquids.
provenance.citation: Hayes, P. J. (1979). In D. Michie (Ed.), Expert Systems in the Micro-Electronic Age. Edinburgh University Press. Hayes, P. J. (1985). In J. R. Hobbs & R. C. Moore (Eds.), Formal Theories of the Commonsense World (pp. 71-107). Ablex.
provenance.locus: Manifesto: clusters of axioms for support and containment; Liquids paper Sections 4-6: contained liquids and what happens when containment fails (spilling).
provenance.notes: The cup-of-water scene: water (liquid) contained in a cup, cup supported by a table, table on the floor (ground). Removing the table breaks the support chain: the cup falls (support axiom) and the water spills (liquid axiom). The floor must NOT fall (ground objects are immobile).

input.intent: predict what happens when the table is removed

expected.notes: Exactly the cup falls (its direct support was removed) and exactly the water spills (its container falls); over-derivation (floor falling) is a defect.
